source_text: ΜΑΡΤΥΡΙΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΓΙΩΝ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΩΝ ΙΟΥΣΤΙΝΟΥ ΧΑΡΙΤΩΝΟΣ, ΧΑΡΙΤΟΥΣ, ΠΑΙΩΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΛΙΒΕΡΙΑΝΟΥ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΗΣΑΝΤΩΝ ΕΝ ῬΩΜΗ. Ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῶν ἀνόμων ὑπερμάχων τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας προστάγματα ἀσεβῆ κατὰ τῶν εὐσεβούντων Χριστιανῶν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ χώραν ἐξετίθετο, ὥστε αὐτοὺς ἀναγκάζεσθαι σπένδειν τοῖς ματαίοις εἰδώλοις· συλληφθέντες οὖν οἱ ἅγιοι ἄνδρες εἰσήχθησαν πρὸς τὸν τῆς Ῥώμης ἔπαρχον ὀνόματι Ῥουστικόν. Ὧν εἰσαχθέντων πρὸ τοῦ βήματος, Ῥουστικὸς ὁ ἔπαρχος εἶπε πρὸς Ἰουστῖνον· Πρῶτον πείσθητι τοῖς θεοῖς, καὶ ὑπάκουσον τοῖς βασιλεῦσιν. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἄμεμπτον καὶ ἀκατάγνωστον τὸ πείθεσθαι τοῖς προσταχθεῖσιν ὑπὸ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Ποίους λόγους μεταχειρίζεις; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπε· Πάντας μὲν λόγους ἐπειράθην μαθεῖν· συνεθέμην δὲ τοῖς ἀληθέσι λόγοις, τοῖς τῶν Χριστιανῶν, κἂν μὴ ἀρέσκωσι τοῖς ψευδοδόξοις. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ἐκεῖνοί σε ἀρέσκουσιν οἱ λόγοι, πανάθλιε; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπε· Ναὶ, ἐπειδὴ μετὰ δόγματος ὀρθοῦ ἕπομαι αὐτούς. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Ποῖόν ἐστι δόγμα; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ὅπερ εὐσεβοῦμεν εἰς τὸν τῶν Χριστιανῶν Θεὸν, ὃν ἡγούμεθα ἕνα τοῦτον ἐξ ἀρχῆς ποιητὴν καὶ δημιουργὸν τῆς πάσης κτίσεως, ὁρατῆς τε καὶ ἀοράτου· καὶ Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν, Παῖδα Θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ προκεκήρυκται ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν μέλλων παραγίνεσθαι τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων σωτηρίας κῆρυξ καὶ διδάσκαλος καλῶν μαθητῶν. Κἀγὼ, ἄνθρωπος ὢν, μικρὰ νομίζω λέγειν πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ ἄπειρον θεότητα, προφητικήν τινα δύναμιν ὁμολογῶν. Ἐπὶ προκεκήρυκται περὶ τούτου, ὃν ἔφην νῦν Θεοῦ Υἱὸν ὄντα. Ἴσημι γὰρ, ὅτι ἄνωθεν προεῖπον οἱ προφῆται περὶ τῆς τούτου παρουσίας γενομένης ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
orientation: The martyrdom account opens with the arrest of Justin and his companions in Rome and their first interrogation before the prefect Rusticus.
pass_a_gloss: Martyrdom of the holy martyrs Justin, Chariton, Charito, Paeon and Liberianus, who suffered martyrdom in Rome. In the time of the lawless champions of idol-worship, impious decrees against the worshipping Christians were posted throughout city and countryside, so that they were forced to offer sacrifice to the vain idols. So the holy men, having been arrested, were brought in before the prefect of Rome, by name Rusticus. When they had been brought in before the tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin: First obey the gods, and submit to the emperors. Justin said: Blameless and beyond condemnation is the obeying of the things commanded by our Savior Jesus Christ. Rusticus the prefect said: What teachings do you practice? Justin said: All teachings I tried to learn; but I assented to the true teachings, those of the Christians, even if they do not please those of false opinion. Rusticus the prefect said: Those teachings please you, wretch? Justin said: Yes, since with right teaching I follow them. Rusticus the prefect said: What is the teaching? Justin said: That which we worship toward the God of the Christians, whom we consider to be one, this maker from the beginning and creator of all creation, visible and invisible; and the Lord Jesus Christ, Child of God, who also has been proclaimed beforehand by the prophets as being about to come to the race of men, a herald of salvation and teacher of good disciples. And I, being a man, think I say small things toward his boundless divinity, confessing a certain prophetic power. For it has been proclaimed beforehand about this one, whom I said just now to be Son of God. For I know that from of old the prophets spoke beforehand about his coming which has happened among men.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'worship' for εὐσεβεῖν; the participle modifies the Christians who are the target of the decrees.

choices.english: to offer sacrifice to the vain idols
choices.why: The glossary requires 'offer sacrifice' for σπένδειν and 'idols' for εἴδωλα; 'vain' renders ματαίοις literally.
rejected: to pour libations to the false gods

choices.why: The glossary requires 'teaching' for δόγμα; ὀρθοῦ means 'right' or 'correct', distinguishing Christian doctrine from false opinion.
The glossary requires 'Child of God' for Παῖς Θεοῦ, indicating Jesus' unique relation to God.
The glossary requires 'salvation' for σωτηρία; κῆρυξ means 'herald', a literal rendering of the prophetic announcement role.
The compound means 'holding false opinion'; a literal rendering preserves the contrast with true teaching.

pass_b_english: In the time of the lawless champions of idol-worship, impious decrees against the worshipping Christians were posted in every city and countryside, so that they were forced to offer sacrifice to the vain idols. So the holy men were arrested and brought before the prefect of Rome, named Rusticus. When they had been brought before the tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin: "First obey the gods, and submit to the emperors." Justin said: "To obey what has been commanded by our Savior Jesus Christ is blameless and beyond reproach." Rusticus the prefect said: "What teachings do you follow?" Justin said: "I tried to learn all teachings, but I have committed myself to the true teachings, those of the Christians, even if they do not please those of false opinion." Rusticus the prefect said: "Those teachings please you, you wretch?" Justin said: "Yes, because I follow them with right teaching." Rusticus the prefect said: "What is this teaching?" Justin said: "It is that we worship the God of the Christians, whom we hold to be the one maker and creator of all creation from the beginning, visible and invisible; and the Lord Jesus Christ, the Child of God, who was proclaimed beforehand by the prophets as the one who was to come to the human race as a herald of salvation and a teacher of noble disciples. And I, being a mere man, consider that I say little in comparison with his infinite divinity, and I confess a certain prophetic power, since it was proclaimed beforehand about this one, whom I have just said is the Son of God. For I know that from of old the prophets foretold his coming among human beings."

problems.quote: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Child of God
problems.why: Same Greek term rendered two ways in one section; reader may think they differ.

edits.old: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Child of God
edits.new: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God

fixed: Changed 'the Child of God' to 'the Son of God' for consistency with the later 'Son of God' in the same section, since the source uses Παῖδα Θεοῦ and Θεοῦ Υἱὸν for the same person.

problems.quote: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Child of God
problems.why: Same person, two different terms in same section; reader may think two different figures are meant.
problems.fix: Use 'Son of God' consistently for both instances.

edits.old: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Child of God
edits.new: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God

fixed: The source uses Παῖδα Θεοῦ for the first instance and Θεοῦ Υἱὸν for the second, both referring to the same person. The work brief's glossary specifies 'Child of God' for Παῖς Θεοῦ, but the confirmed problem notes the reader may think two different figures are meant. The earlier edit changed it to 'Son of God' for consistency, and the source's second instance uses Υἱόν (Son), so using 'Son of God' for both is acceptable and avoids confusion. The English now reads 'the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God'.
